authorization_and_security_scope: All keys are public fixtures: signatures exercise byte binding and verification, not independent task/target authorization, key custody or real demand.

The K*1*64 bound applies only to counted chain-step callbacks at the sole trusted protected owner. Seed queries, signatures, parsing, preparation, cached responses, persistence and transport are additional costs.
Cloning the same policy into another ledger can add capacity. A public-network global cap needs separately established admission/payment/consensus and anti-reset coverage.
Cached receipts are historical, award zero new work and do not revalidate current expiry/reorg context.
The service provides canonical products as preparation assistance; a miner neural-cost lower bound is not established.
Process crash/reconnect and SQLite state are exercised on local tmpfs; power-loss durability and malicious host rollback resistance are not established.
Aggregate query accounting does not prove a positive attacker-owned CPU/GPU/energy/funding lower bound, and says nothing about coherent quantum queries.
